claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has superior plastic strain relative to pure tungsten under high-temperature mechanical loading.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has superior toughness relative to pure tungsten under high-temperature mechanical loading.
The multielement composition of equimolar WTaTiVZr creates significant lattice distortion.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr lowers the effective activation energy for dislocation motion.
Lattice distortion promotes additional dislocation-source formation or activation in WTaTiVZr.
Lattice distortion promotes dynamic recovery in WTaTiVZr during high-temperature loading.
Enhanced dislocation activity and dynamic recovery delay crack initiation and propagation.
High-temperature loading induces enhanced dislocation density in the HEA relative to pure tungsten.
High-temperature loading induces more dynamic-recovery zones in the HEA than in pure tungsten.
Severe lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr reduces the Peierls barrier for dislocation motion.
Pure tungsten has a relatively undistorted and brittle structure compared with WTaTiVZr under the stated loading conditions.
At approximately 1300 °C, the HEA will exhibit greater elongation before failure than pure tungsten tested under identical conditions.
At approximately 1300 °C, the HEA will exhibit greater fracture toughness than pure tungsten tested under identical conditions.
Microscopy after high-temperature loading will reveal more active dislocation sources in the HEA than in pure tungsten.
Microscopy after high-temperature loading will reveal more evidence of dynamic recovery in the HEA than in pure tungsten.
The proposed mechanism is applicable over approximately 1200–1500 °C in inert atmospheres or vacuum and at strain rates relevant to sustained plasma-facing-component service.
Environmental conditions and loading regime can affect the proposed deformation mechanisms.
Sluggish diffusion and secondary-phase formation may contribute to the HEA's mechanical response.
Identically recrystallized HEA and pure-tungsten specimens tested at 1300 °C under the same atmosphere and strain rate provide the proposed controlled comparison.
Failure to observe both improved mechanical performance and enhanced dislocation-source activation or dynamic recovery in the HEA would falsify the proposed mechanism.
